title: How Plants Make Food
summary: Photosynthesis explained simply: sunlight, water and air become food and fresh oxygen.

steps.title: What plants need
sentences: Plants need three main things to make food: sunlight, water and carbon dioxide from the air.
Roots take in water from the soil.
Tiny holes in the leaves called stomata let air in and out.

steps.title: The green kitchen
sentences: Leaves have a green substance called chlorophyll.
Using that energy, the plant turns water and carbon dioxide into a sugar called glucose, and this process is photosynthesis.

steps.title: A gift of oxygen
sentences: While making food, the plant gives out oxygen.
Animals and people breathe in that oxygen.
We breathe out carbon dioxide, which the plants can use again, so plants and animals help each other.

steps.title: Where it goes
sentences: The sugar is used for growing, and the extra is stored as starch in roots, seeds and fruits.
That stored food is what we eat when we eat potatoes, rice or apples.
Without photosynthesis there would be almost no food or oxygen for living things.

facts: The oceans' tiny floating plants, called phytoplankton, make about half of the oxygen on Earth.
Leaves look green because chlorophyll reflects green light.
In autumn some leaves turn red or yellow when the green chlorophyll fades.

quiz.q: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
quiz.why: Plants use carbon dioxide from the air.
Chlorophyll absorbs light energy so the leaf can make food.
